around:Gorges du Verdon & Lac de Sainte-.group: The canyon and the faïence village

old.name: Gorges du Verdon & Lac de Sainte-Croix
old.label: ~1h45–2h drive north (full day trip)
old.hook: Europe's grandest limestone canyon, dropping to nearly 700 m in places, opening onto a turquoise reservoir where you rent a kayak or pedalo and paddle into the gorge mouth.
old.text: Europe's grandest limestone canyon, dropping to nearly 700 m in places, opening onto a turquoise reservoir where you rent a kayak or pedalo and paddle into the gorge mouth. The colour isn't filtered — the Verdon runs milky jade from fluorine, microalgae and fine mineral particles held in suspension. Go weekday and early. The lake basin is man-made, filled 1973–74; it drowned old Les Salles-sur-Verdon, whose last houses were dynamited in March 1974.

old.name: Moustiers-Sainte-Marie
old.label: ~2h north, at the Verdon's gate (just over the line in Alpes-de-Haute-Provence)
old.hook: A Plus Beau Village wedged into a cliff cleft, famous for tin-glazed faïence since the 17th century, with a gilded star strung on a chain between two rock faces.
old.text: A Plus Beau Village wedged into a cliff cleft, famous for tin-glazed faïence since the 17th century, with a gilded star strung on a chain between two rock faces. The star is the village's oldest legend — supposedly hung by a returning crusader as a votive offering. Pair it with the Verdon; the two are one outing. Faïence workshops still fire here.

old.name: Porquerolles & Port-Cros (Îles d'Or)
old.label: 15–35 min by boat from Giens / Hyères port
old.hook: Two of the Golden Islands: Porquerolles for white-sand coves, vineyards and the Fondation Carmignac art foundation; Port-Cros for wild trails and no cars.
old.text: Two of the Golden Islands: Porquerolles for white-sand coves, vineyards and the Fondation Carmignac art foundation; Port-Cros for wild trails and no cars. Port-Cros became France's (and Europe's) first marine national park in 1963 — snorkel its underwater trail. Porquerolles was a 1912 wedding gift from industrialist François Fournier to his wife; the state bought most of it in 1971, and its Conservatoire vineyards preserve heritage vines.

around:Cotignac.group: The hill villages and the wine

old.name: Cotignac
old.label: ~1h10 drive north
old.hook: A Plus Beau Village strung under an ~80-metre tuff cliff riddled with troglodyte dwellings and pigeonniers, ringed by vineyards and plane-shaded squares.
old.text: A Plus Beau Village strung under an ~80-metre tuff cliff riddled with troglodyte dwellings and pigeonniers, ringed by vineyards and plane-shaded squares. The soft tufa rock let villagers carve homes and refuges straight into the cliff — some still accessible. A working wine village, not a museum; it only earned the Plus Beaux Villages label in October 2022. Time it with the market.

old.name: Tourtour & Aups (Haut Var)
old.label: ~1h15–1h30 drive north
old.hook: Tourtour, a Plus Beau Village and 'village in the sky' at 635 m with long views over the Haut-Var; nearby Aups, the black-truffle capital.
old.text: Tourtour, a Plus Beau Village and 'village in the sky' at 635 m with long views over the Haut-Var; nearby Aups, the black-truffle capital. Aups holds one of Provence's great truffle markets every Thursday morning from November to February — Tuber melanosporum, cash only, checked under the nose. Off-season it's a quiet stone village; the truffle is the reason to time it right.

around:Bandol wine country.group: The hill villages and the wine

old.name: Bandol wine country — La Cadière-d'Azur & Domaine Tempier
old.label: ~35–45 min drive west of Toulon
old.hook: Terraced Mourvèdre vineyards climbing between the hilltop villages of La Cadière-d'Azur and Le Castellet, home to Bandol's cult estate, Domaine Tempier.
old.text: Terraced Mourvèdre vineyards climbing between the hilltop villages of La Cadière-d'Azur and Le Castellet, home to Bandol's cult estate, Domaine Tempier. Bandol reds are built on Mourvèdre, a late-ripening grape that only fully works in this sun-trap amphitheatre facing the sea. Tempier — run by the Peyraud family since 1940, whose Lucien is called the 'spiritual father' of Bandol — is the name that made the appellation serious and age-worthy; tastings by appointment, so call ahead.

old_also.name: Domaine Tempier
old_also.hook: The estate that made Bandol serious wine, and whose rosé is one of the Mediterranean's genuinely beautiful drinks.
old_also.text: The estate that made Bandol serious wine, and whose rosé is one of the Mediterranean's genuinely beautiful drinks. This is the terroir story of the Var itself. The Tempier family had held the domaine since 1834; in 1936 Lucie Tempier married Lucien Peyraud and her father gave the couple the estate, which they took over around 1940. Together they fought to win Bandol its own appellation (granted 11 November 1941) and, on 27 October 1943, bottled the estate's first wine, a rosé, instead of selling in bulk. Bandol is mourvèdre country, sun-baked, saline, structured, and Tempier proved it could age for decades. Lucie 'Lulu' Peyraud (1917-2020) was also a self-taught cook whose long feasts became legend; the American writer Richard Olney gave her a whole book, 'Lulu's Provençal Table' (1994), and her disciples Alice Waters of Chez Panisse and importer Kermit Lynch carried her name across the world. The real thing: the pale, mineral Bandol rosé you drink up and down this coast exists in its modern form largely because of one family in the hills above Bandol. Signal Estate in the Tempier family since 1834; Peyrauds drove Bandol AOC (1941); first bottled wine (rosé) 1943; Lulu Peyraud 1917-2020
